subject: FinCo migration compatibility & hyperscaler comparison - next tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Johnson <sam.johnson@finco.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: FinCo migration compatibility & hyperscaler comparison - next tests

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we can get you meaningful data for your migration decision: 

What we heard
- You want an OpenAI-compatible API surface so your product team can swap SDKs with minimal code changes.
- Primary evaluation axes: feature parity (function calls, streaming, chat history), latency and cost at 95th percentile, and prompt-output fidelity (prompt diffs).
- You're running a parallel comparison vs your current hyperscaler endpoints (Bedrock/Vertex) and want clear perf/economics lift estimates.

Proposed tests (what we'll run)
1) OpenAI-compatible baseline: run your representative chat + function-calling prompts against a Redwood-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint using your app's SDK calls.  We'll surface end-to-end request/response differences and token-level cost.
2) SDK swap trial: provide a short code sample to swap the SDK (2-3 files) and a pre-built client package you can drop into your staging environment.
3) Prompt diffs: run your 20 canonical prompts across Redwood vs Hyperscaler X and Y, capture outputs, and run regression checks (exact-match, semantic similarity, hallucination checks).
4) Latency & cost measurement: measure p50/p95 latency, and estimated tokens-dollar cost for 10k and 100k monthly volumes using your profile.

Deliverables and timeline
- Eval plan & checklist (attached) - contains exact prompts, test harness instructions, and data collection format.
- Test environment: we can spin up a short-lived dedicated pool in us-west for the trials; estimate 48-72 hours to provision.
- Proposed timeline: run tests next week (Mon-Wed), deliver initial report by Friday.

Ask for you
- Share the 20 canonical prompts and a short representative SDK snippet (Node or Python) so we can pre-wire the harness.
- Confirm any data residency or compliance needs we should be aware of for the staging pool.

I attached the eval plan PDF and the migration checklist. Connor and Lauren are looped for technical and security coverage - Connor will help with the SDK swap and test harness; Lauren will validate the compliance checklist.

If that works, I'll schedule the provisioning and send a calendar invite for the test kickoff.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
redwoodinference.com

Attachment: 20260618-finco-eval-plan.pdf

From: Sam Johnson <sam.johnson@finco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FinCo migration compatibility & hyperscaler comparison - next tests

Marissa -

Thanks for the clear recap. This looks good. Two quick clarifications: 
1) When you say "OpenAI-compatible" do you mean full parity with OpenAI's chat completions + function calling API (same request/response fields and streaming)? Our front-end team expects minimal change to the request/response parsing.
2) For the SDK swap - will you provide a client that keeps session/KV cache behavior consistent? We rely on a short-term context cache in the client layer.

We can share the 20 prompts and a small NodeJS snippet by EOD tomorrow.

Also, we need the staging pool to be within us-west (no cross-region). Compliance: SOC2 in place is a must; can Lauren confirm audit logs retention?

Sam
Sam Johnson
Senior Product Manager, FinCo
sam.johnson@finco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Johnson <sam.johnson@finco.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FinCo migration compatibility & hyperscaler comparison - next tests

Thanks Sam - quick answers inline and some next steps.

> When you say "OpenAI-compatible" do you mean full parity with OpenAI's chat completions + function calling API (same request/response fields and streaming)?
Yes - our OpenAI-compatible endpoint supports the same request/response fields, streaming chunking, and function-calling hooks. In practice there are two things to watch for: small differences in streaming chunk boundaries and how function call metadata is encoded. We'll capture both in the prompt-diff report and provide a mapper if you need literal field-level compatibility.

> For the SDK swap - will you provide a client that keeps session/KV cache behavior consistent?
Connor: we can provide a drop-in client wrapper that preserves the client-side short-term session cache semantics (LRU TTL) that you described. It exposes the same session API surface Marcus mentioned on the call; the only required change in your code should be the import path and one small initialization snippet.

Compliance/residency
- Lauren: we require SOC 2 (we have the report ready). Audit-log retention for the trial environment can be configured to match your retention policy; we can export logs to your S3 if needed.

Next steps
- Sam: send prompts + SDK snippet by EOD tomorrow (we'll queue it).
- We'll provision a us-west staging pool (48-72h).
- Connor will push the drop-in client and a short migration README to the Drive link: https://drive.company/finco/eval-harness
- Marissa will set kickoff calendar once provisioning is scheduled.

Connor - can you confirm the SDK pack ETA and whether we should include a small Node example that demonstrates function calls + streaming? I added the eval plan and checklist in the Drive folder.

Thanks,
Marissa

--
